labels.updatedIncludesContext: now includes information from the surrounding context
labels.simplifiedNotNumbers: The colours only help us picture the idea. A real model updates many numerical values.

page2.idea1: Focus on one target Token, such as “dog”.
page2.idea4: The diagram is a teaching picture.

page1.title: From context to connections
page1.subtitle: See how available tokens can combine information.
page1.bridgeFromLesson2: Last lesson, you learned that the context window decides which tokens are available to the model.
page1.bridgeForward: Now we’ll explore how those tokens can share information.
page1.isolationBody: Each token can be influenced by information from other tokens around it.
page1.combineBody: When the model processes a token, it can combine useful information from other token positions.
page1.exampleHint: All these tokens are inside the context window. How can they share information?
page1.tokenLabel: The little reader opened the book, shown as six token positions.
page1.flowBody: When processing “opened”, the model can use information from other token positions to work with what is happening in the sentence.
page1.connectionLabel: A conceptual illustration with the tokens The, little, reader, the and book pointing towards the target token opened.
page1.keyIdea: When the model processes a token, it can combine useful information from other tokens in the context.
page1.keywordDefinition: A link between token positions that allows information to be combined from one position with another.
page1.keywordNote: We’ll meet more key words as we continue.

page2.title: How do tokens share information?
page2.subtitle: See how information from different token positions is combined.
page2.heroLine1: The model uses a special mechanism to combine information from different token positions.
page2.heroLine2: This helps each token use information from the surrounding context.
page2.simpleTitle: A simple way to think about it
page2.simpleLine1: When the model processes a token (the target), it can use information from other token positions in the context.
page2.simpleLine2: Different positions can contribute different amounts of information.
page2.tokenLabel: The little reader opened the book, with opened at position 4 as the target token.
page2.connectionLabel: Five arrows point from the other token positions towards the target token opened. Line styles indicate stronger, medium and weaker illustrative contributions.
page2.callout: Different tokens can provide more or less useful information for the current token.
page2.step1Body: The model uses representations from other token positions.
page2.step2Body: Different token positions can contribute different amounts.
page2.step3Body: The information is combined to update the target token’s representation.
page2.resultBody: The target token now has a richer, context-aware representation.
page2.accuracy: Simplified teaching visual — the connections and block heights are not real model values.
page2.attentionDefinition: A mechanism that lets the model combine information from different token positions.
page2.attentionNote: You’ll see how attention patterns can change on the next page.
page2.transformerDefinition: A model architecture used in modern LLMs. It uses attention and other components to process token sequences.
page2.transformerNote: We’ll explore more details in later lessons.
page2.nextTeaser: Next, we’ll discover that not all connections contribute equally.

page3.title: Some connections contribute more than others
page3.subtitle: Compare how much information different token positions can contribute.
page3.heroLine1: When the model focuses on a token, not every other token is equally helpful.
page3.heroLine2: The model can use different amounts of information from different token positions.
page3.focusBody: The model uses information from other tokens to build a better representation of “it”.
page3.explanationLine1: Different tokens can contribute different amounts of information.
page3.explanationLine2: the more useful the information for “it”.
page3.sentenceLabel: Sentence: The dog chased the ball because it was tired.
page3.tokenRowLabel: The sentence shown as ten token positions, with it at position 7 as the focus token.
page3.diagramTitle: How other tokens contribute information to “it” (position 7)
page3.diagramLabel: Six arrows of different strengths point from earlier token positions towards the focus token it at position 7.
page3.keyIdeaLine1: The model combines information from the available context to build a more context-aware representation of “it”.
page3.keyIdeaLine2: This richer representation can later help the model make predictions.
page3.keywordDefinition: A pattern that shows how different token positions contribute information to the current token.
page3.keywordNote: This is a simplified teaching visual, not the exact values from a real model.
page3.whyBody: This helps the model build a representation that reflects more of the current context.
page3.nextTeaser: Next, we’ll see how this information is combined to update “it”’s representation.

page4.title: Position matters too
page4.subtitle: See how token order can change relationships.
page4.heroLine1: The order of tokens affects how information can be combined.
page4.heroLine2: Changing a token’s position can change its connections and the representation built by the model.
page4.whyLine1: The same tokens can appear in different orders.
page4.whyLine2: The model needs information about where each token appears in the sequence.
page4.positionCallout: Position gives the model information about where each token appears in the sequence.
page4.tokenRowA: The dog chased the ball, shown as six token positions with dog at position 2.
page4.tokenRowB: The ball chased the dog, shown as six token positions with dog at position 5.
page4.connectionDiagramA: A simplified comparison with five token positions contributing toward dog at position 2.
page4.connectionDiagramB: A simplified comparison with five token positions contributing toward dog at position 5.
page4.accuracy: Simplified comparison of token relationships — not an exact causal attention map.
page4.positionDefinition: The location of a token in the sequence.
page4.positionalDefinition: Information that tells the model where a token appears in the sequence.
page4.whyBody: Changing order can change the relationships between tokens. Positional information helps the model keep track of those differences.

page5.title: Try it yourself: connect the tokens
page5.subtitle: Explore how positions affect connections. Choose a sentence and a token to focus on. Watch how the pattern of information changes.
page5.chooseFocus: Choose a token to focus on
page5.chooseFocusHint: Select any token to see which earlier positions can connect to it.
page5.noEarlierContext: This first position has no earlier tokens to connect from.
page5.notice1: Different positions can contribute different amounts of information.
page5.notice2: Changing the sentence can change the pattern.
page5.notice3: Choosing another focus token changes it too.
page5.customHint: Type a sentence and discover the connections.
page5.longError: Try a shorter sentence so the connections are easier to explore.
page5.whyBody: Changing token order or choosing a different focus token can change the pattern of connections. These differences can change how the sequence is processed.
page5.tryBody: Switch sentences, choose different tokens, or analyse your own sentence.
page5.accuracy: Simplified teaching visual — deterministic illustrative connections, not real model attention.

page6.title: What happens before prediction?
page6.subtitle: Connect the four stages that prepare context for Lesson 4.
page6.question: What is ready before the model predicts?
page6.intro: Follow the route from available Tokens to the gate that opens next-token prediction.
page6.predictionNote: Processed context is ready to score possible next Tokens.
page6.point1: Tokens inside the Context Window can contribute information.
page6.point2: A Transformer combines information between Token positions.
page6.point4: Contextual processing prepares the model for next-token prediction.
page6.next: Lesson 4 opens the gate and compares possible next Tokens.
